scope: Second two-iteration CP4/FSDP4 rank-32 DROID LoRA smoke with expandable CUDA segments
summary: Expandable CUDA segments removed the earlier all-gather fragmentation failure, but the full attention-plus-MLP LoRA profile still exceeded the two shared GPUs during an MLP adapter forward temporary by 304 MiB.
evidence: The second run progressed beyond the first run's FSDP all-gather failure into the LoRA MLP forward path.
Ranks on physical GPUs 0 and 1 failed at the PEFT lora_B(lora_A(x)) addition for mlp.layer1 while attempting a 304 MiB allocation.
With expandable segments enabled, reserved but unallocated memory fell to roughly 335 MiB, confirming this was a true shared-card peak rather than the prior 1.96 GiB fragmentation artifact.
No optimizer step or checkpoint completed and result.json records PARTIAL.
lessons: MLP LoRA creates a large temporary at the native 93-frame token grid and is the next peak-memory limiter.
Attention-only Q/K/V/output LoRA is a clean quality-oriented reduction because it retains cross-view and temporal attention adaptation while removing the large MLP adapter branch.
limitations: No checkpoint was produced, so the full-target profile has no quality evidence.
next_actions: Version the overlay as attention-only rank-32 and rerun the two-step smoke in a new directory.
